title: The Timeout Decision: Can Sunrisers Hyderabad Interrupt an Opposition Surge?
dek: Can Sunrisers Hyderabad stop an opposition surge by stopping the game? The over that follows a big over shows whether momentum is real.
excerpt: League-wide since 2022, the over after a fifteen-run over has cost more than an average over. Sunrisers Hyderabad concede big overs at a rate the data can compare with the league.
author: CricField Editorial Desk
keyTakeaways: SRH conceded {{ev:to-tbig}} big overs (fifteen runs or more) per hundred overs since 2022; the rest of the IPL conceded {{ev:to-lbig}}.
Across the league, the over after a big over cost {{ev:to-lafter}} runs, against {{ev:to-lavg}} for an average over.

sections.heading: Is Momentum Real?
body: The strategic timeout exists partly to break momentum: after a big over, the bowling side regroups and resets. That only matters if surges carry on, so that a big over makes the next one more likely to be expensive.
Across the league since 2022, the over after a fifteen-run over cost {{ev:to-lafter}} runs, against {{ev:to-lavg}} for an average over. Surges do carry on, at least partly.

sections.heading: Sunrisers Hyderabad's Exposure
body: Sunrisers Hyderabad conceded {{ev:to-tbig}} big overs per hundred since 2022, against {{ev:to-lbig}} for the rest of the league. After those overs, their next over cost {{ev:to-tafter}}.
The fewer big overs a side concedes, the less often the timeout question arises at all.

sections.heading: Using the Break
body: A timeout is most valuable when it changes something concrete: the bowler, the field or the plan for a set batter. Used as a pause without a change, it is a breather rather than a tactic.
For SRH, the practical rule is to pair every reactive break with a specific change, and to record it.

sections.heading: Timeouts Are Not in the Data
body: Public data does not record when timeouts were taken, so their effect cannot be measured directly. The analysis here tests the premise, momentum, rather than the timeout itself.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Break With a Plan, Not a Pause
body: The league evidence supports the idea that surges carry on. Sunrisers Hyderabad should use breaks to change bowler or field, not just to stop the clock.
Logging every break and what changed after it would show whether the decision pays.
